statement: No visible text overlaps other text or is clipped, and no label disappears unannounced. Remedies in order: thin (time, date, numeric and `ordered` category axes only); wrap to at most three lines; rotate up to 45°; truncate in the middle, keeping labels distinct, with the full text in tooltip and table. If labels still do not fit, the note "Some labels hidden. See table." appears and AX143 suggests horizontal bars. The orientation never changes on its own.

notApplicable.compact: Spec 3.7: a compact chart draws marks only, with no axes, tick labels, legend or title, so L1's label remedies, the hidden-labels note and AX143 have nothing to act on. Its only text is a state message (L7) and the C5 corner marker; L1's first clause (no text overlaps or is clipped) still reaches that text, and is routed to L7/compact and A6/compact, where its lack of evidence is recorded.

The 200 % condition doubles the page's inherited font size; the browser's own text-only zoom is not run. The late font is checked at 480 and 1,280 px only, without text spacing or the 200 % condition. No line chart with an unordered category x is drawn in these tests, so middle truncation, the full text in tooltip and table, and the hidden-labels note with AX143 are not exercised on this type.

limits.compact: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. The dash clause concerns lines: compact line, and the edges of compact area, each with two series. For compact bar the bar test compares the painted texture of two series (they must differ in more than 0.1 of the interior), and the model gives them different fill patterns. AX131's level (hint) is read in the browser; its wording (one series) and, for bars, the distinct fill patterns are checked on the model. The lines' colour difference is read as their computed colours, the bars' patterns from the DOM and as painted texture.

limits.line: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. Gaps are read from the SVG path's vertices and from screenshots with the gridlines made transparent; the readouts from the tooltip's text, the table's accessibility tree and the plot's value text. The instant-axis absent step is checked through the controller (Node): AX105, the broken stroke or the "no data" mark, and "No data" in the table and the tooltip.
limits.area: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. Gaps are read from the SVG path's vertices and from screenshots with the gridlines made transparent; the readouts from the tooltip's text, the table's accessibility tree and the plot's value text. The instant-axis absent step is checked through the controller (Node): AX105, the broken stroke or the "no data" mark, and "No data" in the table and the tooltip.
limits.bar: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. The "no data" mark is checked painted for an explicit null on a category axis; at an absent date step and for an absent field it is checked in the Node scene. The readouts are read from the tooltip's text, the table's accessibility tree and the plot's value text. The "F2 bars" describe holds two cases whose titles are chosen by a conditional expression the source scan cannot read (full bar and compact bar); it is cited with atLeast 2, so both must pass. The instant-axis absent step is checked through the controller (Node): AX105, the broken stroke or the "no data" mark, and "No data" in the table and the tooltip.
limits.scatter: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. A point without a y has no position: the tests check that it is not drawn and that the keyboard skips it, so only the table can say "No data". Scatter draws no lines, so bridging, isolated points and absent steps do not reach it.
limits.donut: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. The keyboard reading of null and absent slices is checked in Node; Chrome checks the arcs and the table.
limits.compact: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. The Node tests run compact line, area and bar; a compact chart has no tooltip, table or keyboard reading, so the "No data" readouts do not reach it. The "F2 bars" describe holds two cases whose titles are chosen by a conditional expression the source scan cannot read (full bar and compact bar); it is cited with atLeast 2, so both must pass. The instant-axis absent step is checked through the controller (Node): AX105, the broken stroke or the "no data" mark (compact has no table or tooltip).

statement: Input that cannot be plotted as given is reported, never guessed. The registry in section 3.5 fixes each code's level, delivery, what is drawn and what the reader sees: errors and warnings print once per code per page in every build, hints in development builds only; strict: true throws synchronously from create, update and append for errors and warnings found while validating; late findings are reported, never thrown; data findings name the field and the first row indexes in the caller's form. A value formatter that throws (AX160) shows the reader's note, a tick formatter that throws is reported without one; AX199 covers a throw by Axylo or by author code it runs.

statement: Stacks place positive and negative values on their own sides of zero, and the axis covers both totals. The readout's total is the sum when every component has the same sign; with mixed signs it gives the positive total and the negative total, not their net. A missing component is drawn with zero height and the stack is marked "incomplete" in tooltip, table and announcements. A component is missing whenever its series has no value at that x, a slot it has no row for included (a weekly series stacked with a daily one is incomplete between its rows; owner's decision), and a stacked series' line follows its band.

statement: Donut slices keep the given order, start at 12 o'clock and run clockwise; the legend shows every slice's value and percentage as text, in slice order. A zero slice is listed without an arc, a null slice as "No data". A negative value is AX120 and the chart shows its error state. With more than eight slices that have an arc, the seven largest are drawn and the rest of those are grouped as "Other (n)", with AX121; zero and null slices never count toward the limit and are never grouped; the table lists every category. Shares have at most one fraction digit. An all-zero donut shows the empty state.

statement: Three temporal types, never mixed silently: calendar dates read the same in every viewer time zone; instants (epoch milliseconds declared time, Date objects, ISO strings with an offset) are shown in timeZone (default the viewer's), with the zone named in the tooltip heading and the description; wall-clock times are shown as written, with AX112; instants all on one time of day, whole days apart, raise AX111; a bare number is never taken for an instant.

notApplicable.donut: A donut has category labels and no temporal axis.

F4 line: Date objects read in three local times, name the zone and raise AX111 for whole days (reading: Intl zone aliases name the same zone)

statement: On value axes (y of line, area and bar; both axes of scatter) the zoomed view stays inside the author's domain if given, otherwise inside the automatic domain; after a zoom on x, a y axis with no author domain is fitted again to the values in view. A continuous x of line, area or bar spans exactly its data and the x references it draws (plus half a band for bars), not padded to a tick; so does a date or time x of a scatter, whose numeric x alone follows the tick rule. The automatic domain contains all data, the reference lines and bands the chart draws and stack totals, and ends at the first tick at or beyond each extreme (a compact chart draws no ticks or references: its domain is the same, and reference has no effect there and is reported as not applicable). A field declared percent (0–100) or ratio (0–1) ends at full scale only when its maximum is at least half of full scale and not above it. Nothing is inferred from a label.

Names and descriptions are read from Chrome's accessibility tree. A compact chart shows no heading (section 3.7, C1), so the heading-level part does not reach it.

statement: Keyboard: at most two tab stops while the table is closed, the plot and one toolbar with roving focus that holds legend toggles, zoom, pause and the table control. Every point is reachable in order, the series can be switched, the ends can be reached directly, and focus can leave the chart. The focus indicator is at least 2 px and 3:1 and is not hidden by the tooltip.

notApplicable.compact: Section 3.7 and C1: a compact chart has no tab stop, no toolbar and no keyboard navigation.

gaps.line: The arrow keys are walked through the toolbar at full view only: Pause, which the streaming test finds inside the toolbar's one tab stop, is not reached with them. Nor are the controls shown only while zoomed (Pan left, Pan right, Reset zoom) reached with the arrow keys.
gaps.area: The arrow keys are walked through the toolbar at full view only: Pause, which the streaming test finds inside the toolbar's one tab stop, is not reached with them. Nor are the controls shown only while zoomed (Pan left, Pan right, Reset zoom) reached with the arrow keys.
gaps.bar: The arrow keys are walked through the toolbar at full view only: Pause, which the streaming test finds inside the toolbar's one tab stop, is not reached with them. A bar chart with a date or number x axis, where zoom applies, is not traversed in its zoomed state; the I4 tests show only that its toolbar is the second tab stop and that the arrow keys reach Select range after Zoom in.
gaps.scatter: The arrow keys are walked through the toolbar at full view only: Pause, which the streaming test finds inside the toolbar's one tab stop, is not reached with them. statement: Series are never distinguished by colour alone, in any mode. Each line and area carries a shape marker at its last point and at sparse intervals, repeated in the legend and tooltip; under prefers-contrast: more or forced colours, lines also differ by dash. Adjacent filled marks (slices, stacked segments) are separated by at least 1 px of background. Bars are told apart by position and order and by the legend and tooltip that name them; in a compact chart, which has neither, neighbouring bar series also differ by fill pattern (four patterns exist). The default palette has eight colours, each at least 3:1 on the default light and dark backgrounds, with a minimum pairwise OKLab difference of 0.10 under normal vision and simulated protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia; on any other background AX141 is raised below 3:1.

statement: The chart follows its container with no call from the page, in both directions. With no definite height the plot is 16:9, clamped between 160 and 480 CSS px tall, and the title, controls and table flow above and below it. A container that starts hidden or zero-sized draws when it gets a size.

statement: Light or dark is taken from the chart element's computed color-scheme, else from the luminance of the inherited text colour; --axylo-background overrides both. Marks repaint within one frame when the scheme, forced colours, contrast preference, or the class, style or data-theme of <html> or <body> changes. Forced-colours mode uses system colours.

The titles end in "(Chrome)" but the tests run on every engine. statement: Pointing anywhere in the plot shows what is there, by the type's picking rule (section 3.6), within one frame at the 95th percentile. On line, area and bar the tooltip lists every visible series at the nearest x; a series with no row there reads "No observation", distinct from "No data". The tooltip stays inside the viewport, covers neither the active mark nor any control, can itself be hovered, and lists at most eight rows plus "+N more". A plot narrower than 240 px or shorter than 140 px shows the same content as text in a strip reserved under it; where the strip would leave the plot under the minimum of L8, pointing highlights the datum without a readout. Escape closes it until the pointer reaches a different datum.

notApplicable.compact: Section 3.7: a compact chart has no tooltip, and C1 gives it no pointer-only behaviour.

limits.line: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. Latency is counted in animation frames from the pointer move to the next change of the tooltip or strip, over the 20 probes; P4 covers large data. The hover test rests 300 ms on the datum before moving onto the tooltip (decision 0004, rule 3b). Controls are taken by their boxes (buttons, legend entries, inputs); a control's painted focus outline is checked once, on a line (final-closing). The below-minimum test sets the plot about 100 px high (readout mode, no strip reserved) and reads the highlight from the overlay's marks.

limits.line: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. Motion is traced on the page's clock: each frame's signature of the marks' markup and computed paint (traceMotion keeps only its length and last 120 characters when it is longer) and the animations running on the chart. The 24-chart filter change uses 24 copies of the fixture, without a motion preference, on the machine that runs the suite.

Its criteria are the ones cited as "WCAG x.y.z" in the last column of the specification's criterion rows; a WCAG 2.2 A or AA criterion that no row cites is listed as not covered by a test, with the reason.

The list of WCAG 2.2 A and AA criteria is hand-written in apps/docs/data/wcag.mjs, and no test compares it with the W3C list. Publication with each release has no test. Nor does any test show that a test listed under a success criterion supports that criterion: the page lists every primary test of a spec row under each criterion the row cites.

limits.line: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. Painted checks cover eight series (colours) and nine (colour with dash or marker); six, twelve and 9 to 24 generated series are checked on the drawn scene's marks. The 32 combinations are checked on the scene's marks (each series' colour slot and its dash, marker or pattern; scene.test.ts), not as painted pixels; the painted checks reach nine series (T-limit) and eight colours (A5).

gaps.compact: Pointer input is tried as a move to and a click at the centre of a tile; wheel, drag and touch on a compact chart are not tried in a browser (the model tests show only that the committed frame is not interactive and not zoomable). The pointer probes (a move, then a press and release, on tiles 0, 3 and 39) are judged after all three, by the final DOM and a 900 × 700 px screenshot, so a visible reaction that ends before the last probe would pass. "Nothing inside exposed on its own" lets text nodes inside the image (StaticText, generic, paragraph, none) through: only another role, such as a button or a heading, would fail it.

statement: Memory, measured after forced collection: bytes owned by Axylo beyond the caller's columns for 1,000,000 points at most 1.1 × the caller's two columns (owner, 2026-11-18), and no upward heap slope over 1,000 create–destroy cycles (provisional).

line.title: bounds the retained typed-array backing after opening a million typed observations and appending
line.reason: In Node, the line data store alone: after it opens 1,000,000 typed observations and appends one row, the ArrayBuffer memory it retains is at most 1.1 × the caller's two columns. It counts typed-array memory only, not the rest of the chart (view, scene, DOM, reader), and runs no create–destroy cycles.

line.title: create–destroy cycles show no upward heap trend once the engine has warmed up
line.reason: In Chrome, 2,500 create–destroy cycles of a line chart of the trend fixture: the mean used heap over cycles 2,000–2,500 is at most 1% above the mean over cycles 1,500–2,000, after forced collection. A test with a warm-up and an allowance, not the budget's measurement.

line.title: objects other than compiled code do not grow from cycle 300 to cycle 1,000
line.reason: In Chrome, line charts of the trend fixture: heap objects other than compiled code grow by less than 64 KiB between cycle 300 and cycle 1,000, after forced collection. A fixed allowance between two snapshots, not a slope.

limits.line: Browser evidence: system Chrome, SVG renderer (the default); the citations are answered by Chrome results only, and no Firefox or WebKit result is recorded for this revision. The heap tests collect and measure through the Chrome DevTools protocol.
